libraryPreparationPreflight.agent_guidance: Start the container with `bin/pulsar standalone --no-functions-worker --no-stream-storage` to avoid starting the functions worker and BookKeeper-backed stream storage, which aren't needed for basic producer/consumer coverage and would otherwise slow startup. Expose ports 6650 (client serviceUrl `pulsar://localhost:6650`) and 8080 (admin HTTP, usable for readiness polling, e.g. GET /admin/v2/clusters). Pulsar standalone takes substantially longer to become ready than nats/rabbitmq (it boots a broker, bookie, and ZooKeeper in one JVM), so the test must poll/retry for readiness with a generous timeout rather than reuse the short fixed sleep pattern seen in JnatsTest. Tear down the container (docker kill/rm) after the test so repeated local runs don't leak containers.

deterministic_setup.reason: pulsar-client-all is a network client; exercising producer/consumer/admin paths requires a running Pulsar broker, matching this repo's existing pattern for io.nats:jnats and com.rabbitmq.client:amqp-client. Tag 4.2.5 matches the library version exactly.

risks: Pulsar standalone's startup is slower and more resource-hungry than the other broker images already allow-listed (nats, rabbitmq), which may increase test wall-clock time and flakiness risk under constrained CI resources.

pulsar-client-all is a large shaded jar (~hundreds of MB transitively: netty, avro, protobuf, bouncycastle); native-image build time/memory could be heavier than typical libraries in this repo — no specific blocking GraalVM issue was found during research, but local Gradle/native-image verification remains authoritative.
libraryPreparationPreflight.summary: pulsar-client-all needs a live broker for meaningful producer/consumer coverage; no extra Maven dependency required since the uber-jar resolves its own transitives.
